newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures drift to mostly lower close.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures drift to mostly lower close.

text.p: IMM currency futures drifted to mostly lower closing levels, as the market eyed warily the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, Friday's U.S. January jobs data and Saturday's Group of Seven meeting.
Traders said volumes stayed scanty Tuesday, estimated on the price boards at about 7,200 sterling and 12,000 marks, futures, although action picked up slightly in the afternoon.
Marks slipped to the day's low and approached support near $0.6086, roughly 1.6475 spot, after the U.S. State department said the United States had "no heightened concern" over the situation in Iraq.
The State department declined comment Tuesday on a German newspaper report that the United States is considering a punitive missile strike against Iraq.
The German newspaper said U.N inspectors had found Iraq had continued to develop missiles in contravention of U.N. resolutions ending the 1991 Gulf War.
"It (selling) picked up steam late," said one floor broker. "The dollar had a firm tone...all day."
Brokers said currencies could continue to wander narrowly until Wednesday afternoon, when the FOMC meeting ends and the Fed is expected to make an announcement on any policy change.
"Nobody's going to stick their neck out," added the broker, noting reluctance to trade ahead of Friday's jobs report and Saturday's G7 meeting in Berlin was keeping volumes especially thin.
Recent comments by Japanese officials have made traders think that coordinated intervention is unlikely.

Japan prime minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said Monday the dollar is unlikely to be lowered through international cooperation. Japanese finance minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters Tuesday that Japan does not welcome excessive strengthening or weakening of the yen.
U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin reiterated on Tuesday the United States should not use the dollar as a trade tool.
The mark recouped somewhat versus the Swiss franc after the stronger-than-expected, 1.4-percent rise in December German industrial output.
Sterling gained ground on technicals, its distance from festering EMU jitters, and on crosses, brokers said.

March yen fell $0.000047 at $0.008214, marks eased $0.0019 to $0.6093, Swiss lost $0.0038 to $0.7041, pound rose $0.0090 to $1.6206, Can dollar eased $0.0001 to $0.7463, Aussie dollar lost $0.0011 to $0.7634, Mex peso rose $0.000150 to $0.125475.
